' (' + q.have + '/' + q.need + ')' : '') + (q.status ? ': ' + q.status : '') + (more > 0 ? ' [+' + more + ' other quest' + (more > 1 ? 's' : '') + ' in the journal]' : ''); return q.pos ? { text, pos: q.pos } : text; })()
play.brief: Embervale: an open-world pixel RPG (think Skyrim in pixels). Distances are in tiles. The goal line is the tracked quest and its next step; 'goto goal' walks to where that step happens (a door, a den, a camp). Public buildings are listed by their doors (Inn, Shop, Smithy, Temple...): 'goto Inn' walks in, and inside you talk to the people there (talk Innkeeper) and leave by 'goto Exit'. Entering or leaving a building interrupts the order: give the next one. Stall keepers are talked to from the front of their counter. A newly accepted quest does not replace the tracked one in the goal line (the game says NEW QUEST: ...); every open quest with a place to go is also listed as a Quest thing named by its title: goto "<title>" walks there (a den, a camp, a door). There is no block: fights roll away from telegraphed bites (dodge, the default); wolves wind up before they bite, and a badly hurt one runs off: 'fight' it again to finish it. People can be talked to; animals (hens, dogs, goats...) cannot. Dialogue options are picked with choose N; walking away or choosing FAREWELL ends a conversation. A game call that stays busy (a walk, or a setup call that is still travelling) is stopped with 'call cancel'; the session's own stop ends the whole run.
